solutions.check: 29 entries; each light the paper's grid did not give solved here from its clue's wordplay (an anagram or hidden word, the one listed word fitting every crossing) and its definition (WordNet), as the answer another puzzle gave the same clue, or as the one past answer its crossings left that the printed letters allow, agrees with the 28 answers the paper printed

clue.text: Careless mistakes with house-key

parts.note: slips are small errors
D is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone sloppy keeps making errors with the front-door key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house-key' reads as one object but splits into two pieces: HO for house and D, a musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod work is done without care, slovenly and negligent.

clue.text: Trounce the French doctor as Trotskyite leader

parts.note: la is French for the
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Thrashing a French medic who led a band of Trotskyists.
explanation.walkthrough: MB is the British medical degree Bachelor of Medicine, often used for a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambast someone is to beat or thrash them, or to criticise them harshly.

clue.text: Precipitate slope where branch road starts

parts.note: the pitch of a roof is its slope
a fork is where a road divides and a branch begins

explanation.surface: A steep hill where a side road leaves the highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Precipitate' looks like a noun or adjective but is the verb: to pitchfork someone is to thrust them suddenly into a situation.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitchfork is to hurl or push suddenly into something, which is to precipitate.

clue.text: Left us the new order to hurry

indicators.note: putting into a new order means rearranging the letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to depart in a hurry once things are rearranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new order' rearranges L, US and THE.
explanation.definitionFit: To hustle is to move hastily or push along quickly.

clue.text: In his own words. Gray's expectation of Eton was remote

definitions.text: In his own words. Gray's expectation of Eton was remote

parts.words: In his own words. Gray's expectation of Eton was remote
parts.note: the poet Thomas Gray's ode about viewing his old school from afar, its title read as a hope that was unlikely

explanation.surface: A claim that the poet Gray had little hope for Eton, quoting him.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray wrote 'Ode on a Distant Prospect of Eton College'; read literally, a far-off view becomes an unlikely expectation. Eton is England's famous boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: The title words of Gray's ode also mean a remote chance, an outcome far from likely.

clue.text: Sort of symbol to make art figures pointless inside

indicators.note: a compass point, here E for east, is removed from inside the word for the sculptures

parts.note: statues are sculpted figures in art

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove the points from inside some sculptures.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'point' often means a compass point (N, S, E or W); here the E inside STATUES goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A status symbol is a possession that shows off one's standing, so the answer is a kind of symbol.

clue.text: In a word, it inspired and animated

definitions.text: In a word, it inspired and animated

parts.words: In a word, it inspired and animated
parts.note: put the two letters IN before the answer and that longer word, ..., means inspired and animated, while the answer alone means animated

explanation.surface: A one-word summary of something that inspired and enlivened.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a riddle: IN plus the answer gives INSPIRITED, meaning inspired; the answer alone also inserts IT into SPIRED, the remainder of INSPIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone spirited is lively and full of energy, that is animated.

clue.text: Women's apartments for halma — it is a recreation

indicators.note: a re-creation makes something anew, so the letters of halma and it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Halma, a board game, offered as a pastime in the ladies' quarters.
explanation.walkthrough: Halma is a board game; 'recreation' is read as re-creation, rearranging HALMA and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: In an ancient Greek house the thalamus was the inner chamber or women's quarters; the plural is formed in -i.

clue.text: Little Veronica abandoned by the Pilgrim Fathers

explanation.surface: A girl called Veronica left behind by the founding settlers.
explanation.walkthrough: Veronica is a genus of small blue-flowered plants; the Speedwell was the ship the Pilgrims gave up as leaky, sailing on in the Mayflower alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is the common name of the small veronica flower, and the name of the ship left behind in 1620.

clue.text: Sydney was one of this family — of forgers?

definitions.text: Sydney was one of this family

explanation.surface: A wry question whether the wit Sydney's family were a line of counterfeiters.
explanation.walkthrough: Sydney Smith was a celebrated English clergyman and wit; 'forgers' plays on fraud but means metalworkers at a forge.
explanation.definitionFit: Sydney Smith bore the family name; and those who forge metal are smiths, as in blacksmiths.

clue.text: Partly synonymous baggage!

parts.note: the luggage's name is made of two parts which mean the same thing, both being words for a lawsuit

explanation.surface: A remark about luggage that is somehow half-synonymous.
explanation.walkthrough: SUIT and CASE are both legal actions, so the two halves of the word are synonyms of each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitcase is a piece of travel luggage, and its two halves both mean a lawsuit.

clue.text: One state has room in another for heroes' monument

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state

indicators.note: signals that the word for room is put inside the second state

parts.note: LA is the abbreviation for Louisiana, another US state
a hall is a large room

explanation.surface: A geography riddle about one US state containing a chamber within another, for a memorial to heroes.
explanation.walkthrough: Besides the Norse hall of slain warriors, Valhalla is a hall of fame near Regensburg honouring German worthies.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth it is the hall where fallen warriors feast, and the name was given to a memorial temple for famous Germans.

clue.text: Inserted in page India left out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A printer leaves the word India out when setting a page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' looks like omission, but 'left' gives L and 'out' tells you to rearrange INDIA plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: In bookbinding a leaf is inlaid when it is set into a cut-out in a larger sheet, so it is inserted in a page.

clue.text: Booked gunman with exclusive attitude to women

explanation.surface: A gunman with a booking who keeps women out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Booked' means appearing in a book: Athos is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers. Mount Athos, the Greek monastic peninsula, bars women.
explanation.definitionFit: Athos is a musketeer in a novel; Mount Athos is a monastic community that admits no women.

clue.text: Cheered an unorthodox attachment

indicators.note: unorthodox means not following the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Applause greets an unconventional bond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unorthodox' rearranges CHEERED and AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherence is the act of sticking to something, an attachment or loyalty.

clue.text: In a different way to back her is beset by irreconcilables

indicators.note: signals that the short word to is turned around
beset by means surrounded, so the word is goes inside the pair of opposites

parts.note: West and East are proverbially irreconcilable (never the twain shall meet), giving W and E

explanation.surface: Advice to support a woman in some other manner, though she is surrounded by implacable foes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irreconcilables' stands for W and E, the compass points that never meet; 'back' turns TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Otherwise means in another manner or differently.

clue.text: Knowing it's old hat

explanation.surface: A remark that being shrewd is no longer new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old hat' looks like the idiom for stale, but means an actual hat: the wideawake was a broad-brimmed felt hat of the nineteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone alert and shrewd is wide awake; and a wideawake was a soft low-crowned felt hat.

clue.text: Carriage called for Lady Hester?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a vehicle was summoned for a titled woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Hester Stanhope was a famous English traveller in the Middle East; a stanhope is a light open one-seat carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanhope is a light horse-drawn gig; Lady Hester bore the surname of that family.

clue.text: Finn rests, harassed by hawkers

parts.note: Huck is Huckleberry Finn, Mark Twain's boy hero

indicators.note: harassed suggests being thrown into disorder, so the letters of rests are mixed up

explanation.surface: Mark Twain's hero takes a break but is pestered by street sellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finn' is not a Finnish person but Twain's Huckleberry Finn; 'harassed' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hucksters are pedlars who sell goods aggressively, just as hawkers do.

clue.text: Pudding chosen by George in W.W.I as an example

explanation.surface: Lloyd George picking a dessert during the First World War.
explanation.walkthrough: Cabinet pudding is a British steamed pudding; Lloyd George, Prime Minister in the First World War, picked a small War Cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabinet pudding is a sponge dessert, and a cabinet is the group of ministers chosen by a premier.

clue.text: Poem idly composed by novice

indicators.note: composed means put together anew, so the letters of idly are rearranged

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A beginner dashes off some verse in a lazy way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges IDLY to IDYL, then L for learner (a novice) is added.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a short pastoral poem describing a peaceful rural scene.

clue.text: Where the losers at Gettysburg might have sheltered?

definitions.text: Where the losers at Gettysburg might have sheltered?

parts.words: Where the losers at Gettysburg might have sheltered?
parts.note: the defeated Confederates were General Lee's army, so a sheltered place out of the wind is pictured as his side

explanation.surface: Wondering where the beaten Confederate troops took cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert E. Lee commanded the Confederates beaten at Gettysburg in 1863; the side of a ship or hill away from the wind is the sheltered one.
explanation.definitionFit: The leeside is the sheltered side, and the losing side at Gettysburg was Lee's.

clue.text: No, Sir, nothing has turned up: prayer is needed

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading the words from bottom to top, so they are reversed

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nobody has appeared, sir, so we had better pray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has turned up' reverses NO, SIR and O together, reading upward in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An orison is an old word for a prayer.

clue.text: This is a controversial development, by the way

definitions.text: This is a controversial development, by the way

parts.words: This is a controversial development, by the way
parts.note: a contentious kind of building development strung out along the side of a road, so 'by the way' means beside a roadway

explanation.surface: An aside mentioning some contentious new turn of events.
explanation.walkthrough: Ribbon development is British planning jargon for houses built in a line along a main road, long criticised as sprawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribbon development is housing that stretches along a roadside, a long-debated form of urban growth.

clue.text: Having reached the top in drama school. Joseph died

parts.note: Joseph Surface is the hypocrite in Sheridan's play The School for Scandal

explanation.surface: A drama student called Joseph reached the top before dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drama school' points to Sheridan's comedy The School for Scandal, whose Joseph Surface is a smooth hypocrite; it is not an acting academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has surfaced has come up to the top, as a diver does.

clue.text: One kind of course Germans expressly refuse to complete, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the words are spoken, so we take the sound rather than the spelling

parts.note: Germans say nein for no, and complete means whole

explanation.surface: Germans flatly decline to finish something.
explanation.walkthrough: NEIN, German for no, sounds like NINE, and WHOLE sounds like HOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A short golf course with half the usual eighteen holes is a nine-hole course.

clue.text: Oyster-catcher, mainly mixed type

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the sea
pie is printers' type that has been jumbled up

explanation.surface: A shore bird of a largely mixed kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' looks like 'mostly' but means of the main, the sea; PIE is printing jargon for spilt, mixed type.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea-pie is an old name for the oystercatcher, the black-and-white shore bird.

clue.text: Whole tree in ruins

indicators.note: ruins is a verb here: tree and in are wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: An entire tree lying wrecked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ruins' looks like the anagram indicator, but 'in' is fodder and 'ruins' alone is the verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Entire means complete, with nothing missing.

clue.text: He offers to be considerate about return

parts.note: a tender person is kind and considerate

indicators.note: return means the short word for about comes back to front

parts.note: RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A man offering to be thoughtful about coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' is the reversal signal acting on the short word for about; 'to be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenderer is one who submits a tender, a formal bid or offer.
